body: I don't think we have a strong convention on `render` and `_render`. However I'm thinking that the most useful method is the one that should "public" (not prefixed by _). In this case the most useful would be the one bound to the helper, so maybe we should exhange those two names here.
`actualState === this.removeSearchParameters(helper.getState())` and you don't need to do a `setState`, just keep the reference to the newly created state.
if unmountFn exist, we already that it is a function. We can just test if it's defined.
I'd move that either in its own files or in a dedicated package that is less "everything go". What about "lifecycle.js"?
I like the explicitness, but isn't a bit redundant? Why not `connectConfigure()`
I'd add some tests. This a good opportunity since it's now standalone.
You should extract the function through the render function and also test that the reference is the same at init and render.
Ensure we have a renderFn and an unmountFn if one is specified, they should come by pair.

One way to take a decision on this is to ask ourselves "Is this code already tested by other tests". i.e. if I completely break this module, will tests still pass? If yes then this is an issue and we need to add tests on it. If not, less of an issue but we'd have to discuss about which parts we consider needed for unit tests or not.

As a general rule we can agree that, when moving code around for your own needs, if this code is not tested (our fault), let's add tests to it. Especially since it is not a big function and especially if you are moving this to be reused in a new feature you are developing.

On a side note, this code is probably part mine so I'd be happy to write some tests with you @iam4x in pair, deal? Book some time with me!
